title: Make C# interop less reliant on calling convention/ABI quirks.

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
The C# interop layer uses `uint8_t` arrays on the native side to represent structs passed across language boundaries. This blinds the compiler of what's actually inside those structs, which causes issues when the platform's calling convention promotes one to registers and also has different handling for different types of data.
This exact scenario happened in the linked issue.

This PR attempts to reduce the reliance on the quirks of the platform's ABI by never returning non primitive types as values. (Primitive types are fine since they naturally agree on both sides.) I tried keeping everything uniform and avoided making large architectural changes (since the `godot-dotnet` will replace the built-in integration entirely).

On the native side most functions using these types were immediately casting the pointers to the real native equivalent and they were very rarely used by value, other than to create them on the local stack and attempt to return them. This allowed me to convert them to opaque types and work on removing them entirely. For the most part, this only required the change from the, now `void` aliasing, types to the real type it was being cast to. Some places now benefit from avoiding a copy that was never modified in the first place, other places just got a bit cleaner.
Two types that did get "meaningful" changes are `godotsharp_property_info` and `godotsharp_property_def_val_pair`. They now both own a `StringName` and one a `Variant`, the other a `String`. They are only used in one function in `CSharpScript::_add_property_default_values_callback` now and are never copied, so this shouldn't cause a behavioral change.

Managed side mostly just got the parameters and return type updated, had the call sites adjusted and two got a compatibility wrapper added to `NativeFuncs.extended.cs`, since they were used multiple times in the codebase.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #118138

## Additional information

I tested it myself and tried running as many tests I could find, but I did everything on my x86-64 Fedora KDE 44 Linux machine, I couldn't test other platforms.
